title: Preventing Periodontal Disease: The 2-Minute Daily Habit
summary: Over 80% of dogs and 70% of cats show signs of gum disease by age three. Daily brushing adds years to their lifespan.
bullets: Use only enzymatic pet-safe toothpaste; human fluoride toothpaste is toxic.
Focus on the outer gumline surfaces where plaque minerals deposit fastest.
Complement with veterinary-approved dental chews with the VOHC seal of acceptance.

title: Body Condition Scoring: Evaluating Ribs & Waistlines
summary: Maintaining an ideal body weight reduces arthritis severity, protects cardiac output, and lowers diabetes risks.
bullets: You should easily feel but not see individual ribs without pressing hard.
Look from above: your pet should have an observable hourglass waistline behind the ribs.
Replace high-calorie biscuits with crunchy raw baby carrots, green beans, or dehydrated pumpkin.

title: Recognizing Early Warning Signs of Dehydration & Distress
summary: Knowing your pet's baseline vitals helps you act rapidly in emergency scenarios.
bullets: Perform the 'Skin Turgor Test': gently lift skin between shoulder blades; it should snap back in <1 second.
Check gum color: healthy gums are salmon-pink and refill with color within 1.5 seconds of gentle pressure.
Normal dog resting respiratory rate is 15-30 breaths per minute; cats are 20-30 breaths per minute.

title: Summer Heatstroke Defense & Pavement Safety
summary: Pavement can reach 140°F (60°C) on an 85°F sunny day, blistering sensitive paw pads in under 60 seconds.
bullets: Apply the 7-Second Rule: place the back of your hand on the asphalt for 7 seconds. If too hot for you, it's dangerous for paws.
Walk dogs in the early morning (before 8 AM) or late evening.
Never leave a pet unattended in a parked car, even with cracked windows.
